# Change Audio Pitch

- Route: `/tools/change-audio-pitch`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `audio`
- Slug: `change-audio-pitch`

## Summary

Shift a song or recording by semitones to change its key, lower a vocal, or tune a sample, with the tempo kept the same. (Audio tools)

## Details

A backing track in the wrong key for your voice, a sample that needs to match a song, a vocal that wants to sit a tone lower: pitch shifting fixes all of them. Media Manipulator transposes audio by semitones on our servers with FFmpeg, keeping the duration unchanged, and lets you combine it with a time-stretch when you want the old tape-speed effect instead.
### What it does
- Transposes audio up or down by up to 12 semitones (an octave).
- Keeps the duration the same, so the track still fits.
- Optional time-stretch to change length independently.
- Writes the shifted audio as MP3, WAV, FLAC, M4A, OGG or Opus.
### How to use it
1. Upload audio: Any common audio format.
2. Set the semitones: +2 is preselected; -12 to +12.
3. Convert: FFmpeg resamples and re-times.
4. Download: Save the transposed file.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp3, wav, m4a, aac, ogg, opus, flac, alac, ac3, wma
- Output: mp3, wav, flac, aac, ogg, opus
### Technical details
- The shift resamples by 2^(semitones/12) and compensates the tempo so the length is unchanged.
- Large shifts (more than 5 semitones) on full mixes can sound artificial; vocals and single instruments fare better.
- Formant preservation is on, so a lowered voice does not become a different person.
### Use cases
- Change a backing track key: Move a karaoke track down two semitones.
- Tune a sample: Match a drum or vocal hit to the song.
- Lower a voiceover: Take a read down a semitone.
- Octave effect: Shift +12 or -12 for an effect layer.
### FAQ
Q: Does the speed change?
A: No. Duration is preserved. Use the time-stretch control if you want it to.
Q: How far can I shift?
A: Up to 12 semitones (one octave) up or down.
Q: Will a shifted voice sound natural?
A: For one to three semitones, yes. Larger shifts become audible; formant preservation keeps it from sounding like a cartoon.
Q: Can I shift by cents?
A: Not yet; the control is in whole semitones.
